sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: A rhizomatous perennial horsetail of wet meadows, marshes and ditches. Its upright fertile stems are usually 10–60 cm tall, sometimes reaching 1 m, and bear whorls of branches.

sections.title: Reproduction
sections.text: Like other horsetails, it produces neither flowers nor fruit: spores are borne in a terminal cone on some stems.

sections.title: Toxicity
sections.text: The plant can poison livestock, especially horses and cattle. Alkaloid content varies with conditions and growth stage; do not use it as fodder.
